# Report: judging "The Adventure of the Speckled Band"

**1. The question, frozen.**
The document answers several. The one its title and opening make central: *what killed Julia Stoner?* — and with it, what the "speckled band" was, and what killed Dr. Roylott that same night. Kind: what produces it (forward, from causes). Range: the middle bedroom at Stoke Moran, the two stepdaughters, those nights. Asked: what produced the death.

**2. The jobs, and the parts.**
Jobs, each as a contrast: why Julia and not Helen (yet); why a death with no wound, no poison, nothing found; why a whistle in the dead of night; why the words "speckled band"; why a metallic clang; why a struck match in her hand; why a room sealed at door, shutters and chimney; why the daughters, and why before a wedding; why the ventilator, rope, clamped bed, milk and lash; why Roylott died in that same room. Most are **given** by the client and the coroner. The milk, the lash and the chair are **added** by Holmes himself.

Parts: the swamp adder; the ventilator; the dummy bell-rope; the clamped bed; the saucer of milk; the looped dog-lash; the worn chair-seat; the iron safe; the whistle; the clang; the struck match; the words "speckled band"; the will and its sums; the gipsies; hereditary violence; the cheetah and baboon.

**3. Part by part.**

| Part | Mark | Where it came from |
|---|---|---|
| Swamp adder | **Held**: remove it and no job survives — no wound, no poison, a sealed room, a "band" at the throat | Built: worked out from the room, before the search |
| Ventilator | **Held**: the only route into a locked, barred, stapled room | Built |
| Dummy bell-rope | **Loose**: any line from ventilator to pillow would do. What is held is *a line* — and that it is a dummy, since a working bell would ring and fetch the housekeeper | Fitted to what was seen |
| Clamped bed | **Held**: keeps the sleeper under the rope, and she cannot drag the bed away | Built |
| Saucer of milk | **Two routes**: for the snake, or for the cheetah. Holmes gives the rival reading himself | Fitted |
| Looped dog-lash | **Held**: how else carry a deadly snake to the ventilator and back without being bitten? It is used for exactly that at the end | Built |
| Worn chair-seat | **Held**, as a trace: it fixes how a man reached a high ventilator | Fitted |
| Iron safe | **Held**: the snake's home | Built |
| Metallic clang | **Held**: something clanged. It fails as the shutter bar (the bars were found secured) and works as the safe door | Built |
| Whistle | **Held if**: held only by "he must recall the snake before daylight" — a job Holmes asserts, not shows. Helen says she may have been deceived; the gale and a later hiss both fit the sound | Asserted |
| Struck match | **Held**: it is why a half-seen thing could be named at all | Given by the coroner's record |
| "Speckled band" | **Held**: the rival reading (a band of gipsies) cannot enter a sealed room. The held part is the word's double life — a group, or a stripe on an animal | Given, then sharpened |
| The will | **Held**: why the daughters, and why before a wedding. The sums are worked from the real document | Built |
| Gipsies | **Idle**: remove them and every job is still done. They explain nothing; they only misled | Asserted by the scene |
| Hereditary violence / the tropics | **Loose**: Helen offers both inside three sentences and each does the same work. The answer is already sitting in the starting point | Asserted |
| Cheetah and baboon | **Held** for one job only (why the girls locked their doors); **idle** for the death | Given |

**4. Whole-explanation checks.**

- **Flip.** Had Helen died too, no part would change. Had Julia lived, the same plan-story covers it ("it might or might not bite"). The death explanation is not loose; the *reliability of the plan* is, since it fits a bite and a miss alike.
- **Reverse.** It runs the right way: take the snake away and the deaths stop; suppose the death and no snake appears. Working backward from the sealed room was only how Holmes found it.
- **Answer in the starting points.** "Violence of temper… hereditary in the men of the family" names the thing to be explained and files it under "family."
- **New jobs.** The chair-seat job killed no rival. The milk job killed no rival — the cheetah still stands. The whistle job *helped* the rival it was meant to beat: it is what put Holmes on the gipsies.
- **Pairs that pull.** The whistle must exist (to recall the snake) and must not be heard (or the plot is given away) — and it is the very thing that started the wrong trail. A deadlier snake makes the plan surer and the handler's own room more dangerous; the story settles that pair, the explanation does not.
- **Catch-all.** None in the final version: every part is something Holmes can point at. The gipsies were the bin, and he threw it out.
- **Change list.** Covered and open: a different room (the "repairs" did this), a different sister, a night with no bite, poison (tested and excluded), a man at door or window (excluded by the seals). Left out in silence: whether an Indian snake can be trained to a whistle, come for milk, and climb a rope. The explanation never says.
- **Rival.** "The gipsies did it." The change that separates them is already on the list — put the door, shutters and chimney to the test. The gipsies fail it.
- **Inside.** This explains workings, not just outcomes: the route, the summons, the landing.
- **Remove in groups.** Milk and lash together: the lash keeps its job, the milk loses its only one. Snake and ventilator together: everything falls.

**5. What would make it harder to vary.**
Two things. Show the recall — one change that should matter (the snake returns on the whistle) and one that should not (it stays out under any other sound). And use the milk for something the cheetah cannot also fill.

**6. What this does not show.**
Passing is not truth. This is a story; I judged the shape of the explanation, not whether such a snake exists or can be trained — those are facts to look up, and they sit outside this test. A loose part may still be right.

**7. One next step.**
Take the whistle, the single *held if* part, and write its test. If a snake will not come to a whistle, that part is wrong rather than loose, and the explanation needs a new way to get the snake back.

# Report: The Speckled Band, judged as an explanation

**1. The question, frozen.**
The document answers more than one. The one its title and opening make central: *what killed Julia Stoner?* — and with it, what the "speckled band" was and what killed Dr. Roylott that night. Kind: what produces it (forward, from causes). Range: the middle bedroom at Stoke Moran, the two stepdaughters, those nights. Asked: what produced the death.

**2. The explanation in parts.**
The swamp adder; the ventilator; the dummy bell-rope; the bed clamped to the floor; the saucer of milk; the looped dog-lash; the worn chair-seat; the iron safe; the whistle; the metallic clang; the struck match; the words "speckled band"; the will and the sums; the gipsies; hereditary violence/the tropics; the cheetah and baboon.

**3. Part by part.** (marks per the method; never added up)

| Part | Mark | Where it came from |
|---|---|---|
| Swamp adder | Held: remove it and no job is done — no wound, no poison, a sealed room, and a "band" at the throat | Built: worked out from the room, before the search |
| Ventilator | Held: it is the only route into a locked, barred, stapled room | Built |
| Dummy bell-rope | Loose: any line from ventilator to pillow would do. What is held is *a line* — and that it is a dummy, since a working bell would ring and fetch the housekeeper | Fitted to the room as seen |
| Clamped bed | Held: it keeps the sleeper under the rope, and she cannot move it away | Built |
| Saucer of milk | Two routes: for the snake, or for the cheetah. Holmes himself gives the rival reading | Fitted |
| Looped dog-lash | Held: how else carry a deadly snake to the ventilator and back without being bitten? It is used for exactly that at the end | Built |
| Worn chair-seat | Held, as a trace: it fixes how a man reached a ventilator high in the wall | Fitted |
| Iron safe | Held: the snake's home, and the source of the clang | Built |
| Metallic clang | Held: something clanged. It fails as the shutter bar (the bars were found secured) and works as the safe door | Built |
| Whistle | Held if: held only by "how is the snake recalled before daylight" — a job the explanation asserts, not shows. Helen says she may have been deceived; the gale, and a later hiss, both fit the sound | Asserted |
| Struck match | Held: it is why a half-seen thing could be named at all | Given by the coroner's record |
| "Speckled band" | Held: the rival reading (a band of gipsies) cannot enter a sealed room. The held part is the word's double life — a group, or a stripe on an animal | Given, then sharpened |
| The will | Held: why the daughters, and why before a wedding. The sums are done from the real document | Built |
| Gipsies | Idle: remove them and every job is still done. They explain nothing; they only misled | Asserted by the scene |
| Hereditary violence / the tropics | Loose: Helen offers both inside three sentences, and each does the same work. The answer is sitting in the starting point | Asserted |
| Cheetah and baboon | Held for one job only (why the girls locked their doors); idle for the death | Given |

**4. Whole-explanation checks.**
- *Flip.* Had Helen died too, no part would change. Had Julia lived, Holmes's plan-story covers it ("it might or might not bite"). The death story is not loose, but the *reliability of the plan* is: it explains a bite and a miss alike.
- *Reverse.* The claim runs the right way. Take the snake away and the deaths stop; suppose the death and no snake appears. Backward, from the sealed room and the coroner's blank, was only how Holmes *found* it.
- *Answer in the starting points.* "Violence of temper approaching to mania has been hereditary in the men of the family" names the thing to be explained and files it under "family."
- *New jobs.* Holmes adds jobs as he goes. The chair-seat job killed no rival. The milk job killed no rival — it left the cheetah standing. The whistle job *helped* the rival it was meant to beat.
- *Pairs that pull.* The whistle must exist (to recall the snake) and must not be heard (or the plot is given away) — and it is the very thing that set Holmes on the gipsies. A deadlier snake makes the plan surer and the handler's room more dangerous; that pair is settled by the story's end, not by the explanation.
- *Catch-all.* No ungauged bin in the final version: every part is something Holmes can point at. The gipsies were the bin, and he threw it out.
- *Change list.* Covered and open: a different room (the "repairs"), a different sister, a night with no bite, poison (tested and excluded), a man at the door (excluded by the seals). Left out in silence: whether an Indian snake can be trained to a whistle, come for milk, and climb a rope. The explanation never says.
- *Rival.* "The gipsies did it." The change that separates them is already on the list: put the room's door, shutters and chimney to the test. The gipsies fail it.
- *Inside.* This explains workings, not just outcomes — the route, the summons, the landing.
- *Remove in groups.* Milk and lash together: the lash still has its job, the milk none. Snake and ventilator together: everything falls.

**5. What would make it harder to vary.**
Two things. Show the recall — a change that should matter (the snake returns on the whistle) and one that should not (it stays out on any other sound). And put the milk to a use that the cheetah cannot also fill: feed nothing else that night.

**6. What this does not show.**
Passing is not truth. This is a story; I judged the shape of the explanation, not whether such a snake exists or can be trained — those are facts to look up, and they would sit outside this test. A loose part may still be right.

**7. One next step.**
Take the whistle — the one held-if part — and write the test on it. If a snake will not come to a whistle, the part is wrong, not merely loose, and the explanation needs a new route for recalling it.
